headers.comment: Vite's own output, and ONLY that: bundles and the fonts it emits alongside them. Every one of these names carries a content hash, so a changed file is a changed URL and a year of immutable caching is free. The glob is deliberately narrow — flat files directly under /assets, by the extensions the build actually produces. The woff entries matter: @fontsource is imported through Vite, so the faces land here hashed, and leaving them out of this rule dropped them through to no cache rule at all.

Static media — everything in a subdirectory of /assets. NOT immutable, and that distinction is the whole point of splitting this rule. THESE FILENAMES ARE STABLE: build-1-plot-960.webp keeps its name when the picture inside it is replaced, so the URL cannot tell a browser that the bytes changed. Marking them immutable told every browser never to ask again, and replacing the construction islands with a set at a different aspect ratio left anyone who had already visited rendering last week's image inside this week's box, stretched, for a year, with no way to recover short of a hard refresh. A day of max-age with revalidation after it costs one conditional request per asset per day and answers 304 almost every time. Do not restore immutable here unless the filenames start carrying a content hash.

The handful of media that sit directly in /assets rather than in a subdirectory — logo.svg, logo-mono.svg, icon-rounded.svg, certificate-code.webp. Same reasoning as above: stable names, so they must revalidate. Listed by extension so this rule and the bundle rule above cannot both match a file.
HTML must revalidate so a deploy is visible immediately.

Security headers. The CSP is deliberately strict: no third-party scripts, fonts or connections. There are exactly TWO third-party exceptions, both deliberate, both recorded here. (1) frame-src for Google Maps, which the evidence-record renderings on /platform/renderings embed so the map is the real one the product uses; remove it with those renderings if they go. (2) img-src for tile.openstreetmap.org, which the location-privacy panels on /trust use to draw the same capture at Exact, Nearby and Area precision — see src/components/trust/LocationPrivacyMap.tsx. Both send each visitor's IP to the host concerned. OSM's tile policy asks that production services not run on their donated infrastructure, so if traffic grows, point TILE_URL at a paid provider and narrow this entry to that host. If analytics are added, widen script-src and connect-src for that host ONLY, rather than relaxing the policy.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https://tile.openstreetmap.org; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-src https://www.google.com https://maps.google.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests
